warnings: Phosphorus is in almost every food; most healthy people reach the target from normal meals and do not need a supplement.

Phosphate additives (phosphoric acid, phosphates, E338 to E341, E450 to E452) in colas, processed cheese and processed meats are absorbed almost completely and are not shown on Indian food labels as phosphorus.

If you have kidney disease of any stage, your doctor or renal dietitian sets your phosphorus limit. Follow your doctor's advice. Do not take phosphorus supplements, phosphate laxatives or enemas unless your doctor prescribes them.
Sodium phosphate laxatives and enemas can cause acute kidney injury, especially with dehydration or kidney disease, or with diuretics, ACE inhibitors, ARBs or NSAIDs.
If you have eaten very little for several days or weeks, ask a doctor before returning to normal meals (refeeding risk).
Upper limit 4,000 mg/day for adults (3,000 mg over age 70) from US NASEM; ICMR upper limit not found.
General information, not medical advice. Check with a doctor before starting supplements.
